title: Rates and macro snapshot as of the 2024-09-19 close
text:
Rates and macro snapshot as of the 2024-09-19 close. Compiled from public sources: U.S. Treasury constant-maturity yields (FRED DGS1, DGS2, DGS3, DGS5, DGS7, DGS10, DGS20, DGS30). All levels are as of the 2024-09-19 close.

Monetary policy. On 2024-09-18 the Federal Open Market Committee lowered the target range for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 4-3/4 to 5 percent - the first reduction of this cycle, and a larger-than-standard first step. The statement said the Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent and judges the risks to its employment and inflation goals to be roughly in balance. Governor Bowman dissented, preferring a 25 basis point reduction. The accompanying Summary of Economic Projections shows a 4.4 percent median federal funds rate for end-2024 (implying about 50 further basis points of cuts across the two remaining 2024 meetings) and 3.4 percent for end-2025 - a gradual projected path that is shallower than an aggressive easing cycle.

Positioning context. Treasury yields had already fallen substantially into this meeting as markets priced an easing cycle: the 2-year yield ended 2024-09-19 at 3.59 percent, roughly 120 basis points below its 4.77 percent close on 2024-07-01, and the 2s10s spread recently turned positive after a long inversion. Market-implied paths going into the meeting were more aggressive than the Committee's own projected path. The next scheduled FOMC meeting concludes 2024-11-07; the U.S. general election is scheduled for 2024-11-05, inside the inter-meeting window.
